subject: Qualification: PoC trial plan & deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: alex.johnson@acmecorp.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Qualification: PoC trial plan & deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Alex — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we put the PoC plan in motion.

Recap of Acme requirements (as discussed):
- Primary use: customer-facing chat and summarization across support tickets (real-time).
- Throughput target: ~150 concurrent users initially, peak bursts to ~600 qps for short periods.
- Latency SLO: ~100ms 95th for short chat prompts; acceptable up to 150ms during peaks.
- Data residency & compliance: US-only data residency; SOC 2 / audit logs required; KMS for customer-encrypted data; SSO integration (SAML).
- Budget sensitivity: want predictable unit costs; prefer not to provision large reserved fleets unless justified.

Deployment mode options we discussed and recommended approach:
1) Hosted API (fastest time-to-value): Redwood-hosted, SOC2, supports customer-managed KMS for keys. Good for rapid validation and product-led rollout.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): predictable throughput, isolated capacity, VPC peering. Best if you need consistent p50/p95 latency under sustained load.
3) Private VPC / On-prem: full control for regulated or air-gapped environments. Longer lead time (infra + networking + compliance).

Recommendation: Start with a short Hosted trial to validate integration and accuracy with your data, then evaluate a quick switch to Dedicated if we see sustained throughput/latency needs or you prefer isolated capacity. Private deployment typically comes later for strict regulatory or procurement constraints.

PoC success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: <= 150ms 95th under a scripted load that simulates 150 concurrent users (burst to 600 qps).
- Availability: >= 99% during test window.
- Functional: end-to-end integration with your SSO + KMS; model outputs meet quality thresholds on a shared eval set (we’ll define pass/fail thresholds).
- Cost: estimate within the budget band discussed (we’ll confirm token-based costing for the trial).

Proposed timeline:
- Kickoff: week of Apr 19 (1-hour technical kickoff)
- Integration & baseline tests: Apr 20–23
- Load/quality evaluation: Apr 24–26
- Review & next-step decision: Apr 28

Next steps for you: please confirm 1) preferred deployment mode to start (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), 2) list of stakeholders we should include on the kickoff (technical, security, procurement), and 3) any blackout dates next week.

I’ve attached a one-page PoC trial plan and a link to the shared folder with test scripts and an integration checklist.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa to coordinate schedule and Lauren from CS for success criterion sign-off.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Alex — great, thanks for the quick reply and the stakeholder list. Answers inline and attached PoC document.

Compliance & deployment notes:
- Hosted: Redwood’s hosted API is SOC 2 Type II and we support customer-managed KMS for model payload encryption and envelope keys. We can provide audit logs and a compliance pack for PoC. For SSO we support SAML/Okta; we’ll need one test SSO user.
- Dedicated: Dedicated capacity provides isolated GPU pools and optional VPC peering for private networking. It’s the sweet spot if you need consistent p95 latency without moving to full Private.
- Private: longer lead time (4–8 weeks typical) for on-prem or air-gapped deployments; good for highly regulated final production.

Procurement / cost: I’ve included a ballpark in the attached PoC (see section 3). Short answer: Hosted trial usage pricing for the PoC will be metered; Dedicated estimates are in the attached doc (monthly reserved commit scenarios). We’ll share a more formal quote pending which deployment mode you want to pursue after PoC.

Proposed kickoff & test schedule (updated):
- Technical kickoff (30–60m): Apr 19 — introduce teams, confirm test dataset and SSO/KMS steps.
- Integration & baseline: Apr 20–22 — integration + functional checks.
- Load & quality tests: Apr 23–25 — scripted load runs and evaluation on your eval set.
- Review: Apr 26 — joint review & next-step decision.

I’ve attached the PoC plan (Redwood_PoC_Trial_Plan_AcmeCorp_v1.pdf) that includes test scripts, roles/responsibilities, and the ballpark cost table. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPoCPlan

Alex / Ben — looping in the CS perspective and explicit success criteria we’ll validate during the PoC.

CS PoC validation checklist (we’ll sign off these during the review):
- Latency: <=150ms 95th under the scripted load (we’ll provide the JMeter script).
- Throughput: sustain 150 concurrent with bursts to 600 qps without >=5% error rate.
- Functional: SSO sign-in, KMS key rotation verification, and audit log completeness.
- Quality: model meets the pass rate of >= 85% on the shared eval set (we’ll agree on the dataset beforehand).
- Operational: ability to rotate API keys and revoke access within 1 minute; monitoring alerts firing for p95 spikes.

What we need from Acme before kickoff:
1) A technical point-of-contact for Samir’s team who can approve SSO/KMS test accounts.
2) A representative sample of 200–500 anonymized user prompts for the quality eval (or permission to use synthetic data).
3) Any networking restrictions we should be aware of for VPC peering (if you later opt for Dedicated).

I’ll schedule the technical kickoff on Apr 19 (30 minutes) and send a calendar invite once you confirm a time window. Marissa will coordinate logistics.

Thanks,
